title: Developer Enablement Initiative — Cross-cycle Playbook & Signal Automations
creator: Aanya Patel
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, cross-cycle playbook and signal automation pipeline that reduces developer time-to-first-success for Redwood SDKs, docs, and quickstarts by 30% (activation metric) and drives a 15% lift in 7-day retention for self-serve projects.

Scope:
- Author a modular playbook that covers: quickstart sequencing, canonical code snippets for JS/Python, recommended prompts/examples, and guardrails for structured output and function-calling.
- Instrument SDKs and quickstarts with event telemetry and a signal contract so the Console can surface activation funnels (first API call, token usage, successful inference responses).
- Build alerting and a visualization dashboard (activation funnel, TTFCall distribution, common error map, platform latency buckets) and automate weekly signals that feed into the DevX OKR dashboard.
- Ship a rollout kit for Growth/SEs: copy-ready emails, in-product banners, and a small set of onboarding templates for common integrations (chat, summarization, embeddings).

Success measures:
- Primary: time-to-first-success (median) reduced by 30% within two cycles after rollout.
- Secondary: 15% increase in 7-day retention for projects created via quickstarts in target segments; 20% decrease in support tickets labelled "first-call failure" for SDKs.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence) with modular tasks and owners.
- Instrumentation spec (telemetry events + schema) for ENG to implement (ENG-12821).
- Dashboard in Looker/Metabase + weekly automation job that emits signal summaries to #devx-okrs.
- 3 quickstart templates (JS server, Python script, Serverless function) with canonical prompts and CI-smoke tests.

Approach and trade-offs:
- We will prioritize high-traffic quickstarts first (JS SDK server template, docs for embeddings). Lower-traffic languages go into Phase 2. This balances impact vs engineering bandwidth.
- To reduce friction, initial telemetry will be minimal (events: quickstart_started, first_api_call_success, quickstart_completed, quickstart_error) with enrichment deferred to Phase 2 to avoid long telemetry implementation cycles.
- We will avoid inline SDK code changes that could break backward compatibility; where necessary use feature flags and deprecation windows.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aanya Patel (owner)
- Engineering leads: Priya Sharma (SDKs) and Marcus Lee (Telemetry)
- Design: Nia Gomez (UX for quickstart flows)
- Growth/CS: Helena Ruiz (rollout kit)
- Observability: Platform Analytics (dashboard build)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Telemetry schema drift across SDKs. Mitigation: central schema repo + CI validation in PRs.
- Risk: Dashboards misinterpret noisy signals. Mitigation: add smoothing/percentile views and label confidence levels.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1–2: Playbook draft + telemetry event contract; design wireframes for quickstart flow.
- Week 3–4: ENG implement telemetry in JS + Python quickstarts; dashboard scaffold.
- Week 5: Pilot internal teams + growth cohort; collect signals and iterate.
- Week 6–8: External rollout, monitor OKRs, and prepare Phase 2 backlog (additional languages, richer enrichment).

Notes: This initiative is intentionally cross-cycle: measurable impact expected within two release cycles, but the playbook and automation are permanent assets that will be maintained by DevX and Platform Analytics.
